newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic developing pacemaker for Asia.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic developing pacemaker for Asia.

text.p: With an eye on new markets, Medtronic Inc is developing a low-cost pacemaker exclusively for sale in China, India and other developing Asian nations.
The simple, inexpensive Champion model is set for release in February or March next year, said Steve Harrison, a marketing manager on the project, in an interview Wednesday.
The Champion will sell for less than the current average Chinese pacemaker price of about $1,200, he said.
The units will be made at a $10-million factory and office complex Medtronic is constructing in Shanghai.
The complex will be the first wholly foreign-owned pacemaker plant in China and represents a modest, but potentially lucrative wager on Asian growth, analysts said.

"Emerging markets like China, India and similar countries in that part of the world have sizable populations that represent important new growth opportunities for companies like Medtronic," said Cowen & Co analyst Michael Mullen.
"Most companies in the medical technology industry have been looking for ways to legitimize moves into these markets because the big issue is how you get paid," Mullen said.
Only a fifth of China's population has healthcare coverage of any sort. But since the Chinese population is 1.2 billion, that small fraction represents a huge market, Mullen said.
"There is a sizable middle and upper class that exists now in China and is growing rapidly, and also in India and these other countries," he said.
Although common in the Western world and Japan for treating slow or irregular heartbeats, pacemakers remain a rarity in developing countries, Medtronic said.
In the United States, where a pacemaker costs about $6,000, about 550 people per million have a pacemaker implant.
In Hong Kong, the rate is 200 per million, Harrison said.
In China, with a population of 1.2 billion, there are only three to four pacemaker implants per million. Implant rates in India and other Asian nations are also low.
The total Chinese pacemaker market today is about 4,500 units per year and Minneapolis-based Medtronic has about 30 percent of it, Harrison said.

Competition from St. Jude Medical Inc and others is intense, he said, and some local competitors are emerging. But he added that Medtronic is not aware of any rival developing a market-specific product like the Champion.
Medtronic holds 51 percent of the $2.4-billion global pacemaker market. Its shares were up 7/8 to 62-5/8.
